'''Lisa Barsotti''' is a principal [[research scientist]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] [[Kavli Institute]] at the LIGO Laboratory, beginning her career in 2010.

==Biography==
Barsotti was born June 1,1978 and was raised in Pisa, Italy. She obtained her PhD in [[applied physics]] from [[University of Pisa]] in 2006 on ''The control of the [[Virgo interferometer]] for [[gravitational wave]] detection'' and moved to the United States in 2007 to work on the [[Laser Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory]] (LIGO).<ref name="inspiringfifty">{{Cite web|url=https://italy.inspiringfifty.org/lisa-barsotti|title=Lisa Barsotti|website=Inspiring Fifty: Italy|access-date=1 January 2023|archive-date=1 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230101190345/https://italy.inspiringfifty.org/lisa-barsotti}}</ref>

Barsotti was involved in the discovery of gravitational waves reported in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ksj.mit.edu/news/2020/03/13/lisa-barsotti-seminar/|title=The Chirp Heard 'Round the World: LIGO's Lisa Barsotti Reflects on a Landmark Discovery|author=Zain Humayun|date=13 March 2020|website=Knight Science Journalism @MIT}}</ref>

She currently investigates technology to improve [[gravitational wave detection]] using squeezed states of life,<ref>{{cite journal | arxiv=1310.0383 | doi=10.1038/nphoton.2013.177 | title=Enhanced sensitivity of the LIGO gravitational wave detector by using squeezed states of light | date=2013 | last1=Aasi | first1=J. | last2=Abadie | first2=J. | last3=Abbott | first3=B. Main themes of her work include astronomy, remote sensing, optics, interferometry, laser, [[electric field]], and sensitivity. 

Reflecting on her work, she has expressed that, even in the years before detections were made, she found fulfillment in the challenge of utilizing highly sophisticated instruments and contributing to the understanding of Einstein's Theory of [[General relativity|General Relativity]]. She admires the hard work and diverse knowledge of those she's worked with. She views the prize as a recognition of the collective efforts of scientists worldwide who have pushed the boundaries of gravitational wave research.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Breakthrough Prize – Fundamental Physics Breakthrough Prize Laureates – Lisa Barsotti |url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/1/L3833 |access-date=2025-03-17 |website=breakthroughprize.org |language=en}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
*2018 – [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] for "extraordinary leadership in commissioning the Advanced LIGO detectors, improving their sensitivity through implementation of squeezed light, and enhancing the operation of the gravitational wave detector network through joint run planning between LIGO and Virgo"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org}}</ref>
*2019 – [[Breakthrough Prize|Breakthrough]] [[New Horizons in Physics Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/1/L3833|title=Breakthrough Prize – Fundamental Physics Breakthrough Prize Laureates – Lisa Barsotti|website=breakthroughprize.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Ho7pVGucOA|title="I'm doing something that is bigger than me": Lisa Barsotti on being a scientist|date=7 August 2019 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref>
*2019 – [[Capperuccio Prize]] of the city of [[Livorno]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.telegranducato.it/2019/06/26/premio-capperuccio-a-lisa-barsotti/|title=Premio Capperuccio a Lisa Barsotti|first=Anna|last=Romano|date=26 June 2019|website=Telegranducato di Toscana}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.comune.livorno.it/articolo/premio-capperuccio-lisa-barsotti|title=Il Premio Capperuccio a Lisa Barsotti|date=24 June 2019|website=Città di Livorno}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.livornotoday.it/attualita/premio-capperuccio-lisa-barsotti-lions-livorno.html|title=Capperuccio, il Lions Club Porto Mediceo premia Lisa Barsotti|website=LivornoToday|date=4 June 2019}}</ref>
*2021 – One of InspiringFifty in Italy<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://italy.inspiringfifty.org/italy-2021-1|title=Italy 2021|website=Inspiring Fifty: Italy|date=2021|access-date=1 January 2023|archive-date=16 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230316084428/https://italy.inspiringfifty.org/italy-2021-1}}</ref>
*2022 - [[Research.com]] Best Female Scientist Award
*2023 - [[Research.com]] Best Female Scientist Award
*2024 - [[Research.com]] Best Female Scientist Award{{cn|date=May 2025}}
